name: Zipline
description: Zipline is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors, funds and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Zipline is a privately held drone delivery company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $1.5 billion round announced on November 5, 2026, valued the company at $21.5 billion.

Based in South San Francisco, California, Zipline designs, builds and operates autonomous aircraft that deliver meals, retail orders and medical supplies in the United States, several African countries and Japan. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
figs: Special purpose vehicles with SEC filings naming Zipline
Shares reported by ARK Venture Fund (July 31, 2026)
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round, except the Series G valuation, which Bloomberg reported in January 2026. The Series H combines more than $600 million raised in January 2026 with $200 million added in March; Zipline did not announce its 2024 Series G, and the Series F figures are as reported by Forbes.
round_notes: Zipline has said the proceeds of the November 2026 round will fund the expansion of its manufacturing and hiring in the United States. In the same announcement, the company said it had completed more than one million deliveries in the Dallas-Fort Worth area during 2026; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global led the November 2026 round, with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest and Salesforce Ventures. Fidelity, Baillie Gifford, Valor Equity Partners and Tiger Global invested in the Series H, which Paradigm joined in March 2026, and Baillie Gifford led the Series E. Other investors include Temasek, Katalyst Ventures, Intercorp and Emerging Capital Partners.
spv_sentence: Since 2025, 10 special purpose vehicles formed to invest in Zipline have filed with the SEC, seven of them in 2026.
funds: Mutual funds and other SEC-registered funds managed by Fidelity, Capital Group and ARK Investment Management reported Zipline holdings in filings for periods in 2026. As of July 31, 2026, ARK Venture Fund held 327,237 shares, which it valued at $20.6 million, or $63.01 per share.
sources: Sources: Zipline's announcements of its November 2026 financing and January 2026 financing; reports by TechCrunch (November 2026, March 2026 and June 2021), Bloomberg (January 2026), Forbes (April 2023) and FreightWaves (May 2023); ARK Venture Fund's Form N-PORT for July 31, 2026; and SEC Form D and Form N-PORT filings.
